facts.fact: The US-Uganda health MOU signed 10 December 2025 names eAfya and ClinicMaster as the Government of Uganda's Electronic Medical Records and has the Government leading the national EMR scale-up, approving the national health information architecture before any US-financed investment and owning all data generated.

The MOU, running 1 April 2026 to 31 December 2030, sets out a national EMR scale-up naming eAfya and ClinicMaster: a functional EMR in all facilities down to Health Centre III by 2028, national registries and EMR governance structures finalised by December 2026, and 80% of encounters entered in real time within one year of rollout and 90% within two.

Under the MOU the US Government plans US$113,102,289 for data systems over 2026-2030, including support for the national EMR scale-up, while the Government of Uganda only plans to allocate domestic resources to assume EMR maintenance gradually over the five years; no existing domestic budget line is stated.
